scenarios.hypothesis: An outer synthetic withdrawal exposes transient accounting before an external callback re-enters a second function that shares the same invariant and consumes the not-yet-committed state.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A local test chain with depth-1 synthetic callback, bounded test balances, shadow ledger, and read-only state snapshots records only inert accounting markers.
scenarios.positive_control: The same withdrawal with accounting committed before the external call prevents the second function from observing a stale balance and preserves the shared invariant.
scenarios.negative_control: The same callback target with reentry disabled returns normally and the outer withdrawal completes with no duplicate or stale-state marker.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would deploy against a live protocol, move real assets, use unbounded recursion, grief gas/resources, or leave the owned local test chain.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After moving the relevant state update before the external call or adding invariant-scoped protection, the callback path cannot consume transient accounting while normal withdrawal still succeeds.
scenarios.outer_transaction_callback_generation: Record deployment, outer actor, withdrawal transaction generation, outer call frame, callback target generation, reentry generation/depth, and final commit generation.
scenarios.external_call_reentrant_entry_trace: Bind the withdrawal external-call site, callback trigger, second-function reentrant entrypoint, parameters, and the exact state visible to the reentrant frame.
scenarios.transient_state_update_ordering: Capture expected accounting update order, actual writes before callback, deferred writes after return, transient balance generation, and first reentrant consumption.
scenarios.lock_guard_invariant_scope: Record guard identity/generation, functions covered, shared accounting invariant domain, and prove whether the second function is inside or outside effective protection.
scenarios.cross_function_contract_hook_lineage: Classify the path as cross-function callback within the same protocol state domain and record callback contract identity plus reentrant function lineage.
scenarios.outer_continuation_commit_state: Trace outer continuation after callback return, any stale assumptions reused, remaining ledger writes, final commit, and resulting invariant state.
scenarios.downstream_protocol_consumer_identity: Identify the local shadow-accounting consumer that accepts the reentrant state and emits a deterministic read-only receipt for the same transaction generation.
scenarios.effective_reentrancy_state_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one bounded local cross-function acceptance against transient synthetic accounting state during a depth-1 callback.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is an inert local accounting marker and receipt showing outer/reentrant generations, transient balance state, and no real asset or production effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate deployment, outer transaction, call frames, callback trigger, transient state, guard scope, reentrant consumer, outer commit, and receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold deployment, actor, amount, callback target, invariant, and consumer constant while changing only state commit timing before versus after the external call.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject different transaction generations, callback mock contract drift, permitted transient accounting, outer-frame revalidation, wrong invariant scope, or receipt from another chain reset.
scenarios.evidence_level: SCR4 because a reversible local accounting marker is causally bound to one cross-function depth-1 callback consuming transient state before outer commit.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SCR4 maximum until complete frame provenance, alternative elimination, deterministic remediation replay, and regression evidence satisfy the SCR5 contract.

scenarios.hypothesis: A reentrancy guard protects the outer function but not a second entrypoint that mutates the same synthetic accounting invariant, allowing callback-time cross-function state access.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled local test chain uses a fake callback contract, bounded test ledger, guard-state receipts, and no transferable assets or external production interaction.
scenarios.positive_control: An invariant-scoped guard covering both entrypoints blocks the callback-time second function while preserving normal sequential calls after the outer transaction finishes.
scenarios.negative_control: The original per-function guard correctly blocks same-function reentry, proving the defect is cross-function invariant coverage rather than a nonfunctional guard.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would deploy against a live protocol, move real assets, use unbounded recursion, grief gas/resources, or leave the owned local test chain.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After extending protection to the complete invariant scope or introducing equivalent state-phase gating, the cross-function callback is denied while allowed post-commit calls still succeed.
scenarios.outer_transaction_callback_generation: Record outer transaction/call-frame generation, guard generation, callback generation, reentrant second-function frame, and final commit/guard-release generation.
scenarios.external_call_reentrant_entry_trace: Bind the exact external call, callback trigger, second reentrant entrypoint, observed guard state, parameters, and shared state generation.
scenarios.transient_state_update_ordering: Record the transient shared-ledger state exposed during callback, deferred outer updates, reentrant mutation attempt, and post-callback commit order.
scenarios.lock_guard_invariant_scope: Map the per-function guard to the outer entry only, the second function outside its scope, and the shared invariant fields both functions can mutate.
scenarios.cross_function_contract_hook_lineage: Classify the path as cross-function reentry through the synthetic callback and bind outer function, callback target, and second entrypoint identities.
scenarios.outer_continuation_commit_state: Capture whether the outer frame continues after the second-function marker, which assumptions it reuses, final ledger state, and guard release.
scenarios.downstream_protocol_consumer_identity: Identify the local shared-ledger consumer that records the second-function callback-time action and emits the guard-scope receipt.
scenarios.effective_reentrancy_state_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one inert second-function action against a shared invariant while only the outer function's guard is active.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a reversible local ledger marker and guard-scope receipt with no live protocol, asset, governance, or gas-griefing effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind outer transaction, guard state, callback frame, second-function frame, shared invariant generation, outer continuation, final state, and receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold deployment, callback, shared ledger, actor, and outer flow constant while changing only per-function versus invariant-scoped guard coverage.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject independent authorization for the second function, different state domain, same-function-only invariant, callback mock drift, or marker emitted outside guard lifetime.
scenarios.evidence_level: SCR4 because a bounded second-function marker is accepted during the outer guard lifetime and is causally tied to insufficient invariant-scope protection.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SCR4 maximum until full guard-generation provenance, alternatives, receipts, and remediation regression justify SCR5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A fake hook-enabled token triggers a depth-1 callback before the protocol commits its internal synthetic balance update, allowing the callback to observe and act on the old balance generation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A local test chain with a fake hook token returning fixed inert markers, bounded balances, and read-only snapshots exercises only one controlled callback.
scenarios.positive_control: Committing the internal balance state before invoking the hook-enabled token causes the callback to observe the current balance generation and no stale-state marker.
scenarios.negative_control: Using the same fake token with hook callback disabled preserves the original operation and produces no reentrant entry or marker.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would deploy against a live protocol, move real assets, use unbounded recursion, grief gas/resources, or leave the owned local test chain.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After update ordering is corrected or callback exposure is isolated, the depth-1 hook observes current state while normal token interaction remains functional.
scenarios.outer_transaction_callback_generation: Record actor, outer operation transaction, call frame, fake token generation, hook callback generation, reentry depth, and final commit generation.
scenarios.external_call_reentrant_entry_trace: Bind token-call site, hook trigger, callback target, reentrant entrypoint, observed internal balance, and exact callback parameters.
scenarios.transient_state_update_ordering: Capture old balance generation, intended new balance, external token call before commit, hook-time observation, deferred write, and outer commit.
scenarios.lock_guard_invariant_scope: Record any guard/phase state and whether it protects the balance invariant across token-hook callback execution and reentrant entrypoints.
scenarios.cross_function_contract_hook_lineage: Classify the path as hook-enabled token callback and bind protocol contract, fake token, hook receiver, and any reentrant function lineage.
scenarios.outer_continuation_commit_state: Trace outer continuation after hook return, internal balance write, revalidation behavior, terminal commit, and final invariant result.
scenarios.downstream_protocol_consumer_identity: Identify the local callback-time balance consumer that records the stale-generation observation and any inert protected marker.
scenarios.effective_reentrancy_state_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one depth-1 synthetic hook callback observing or acting on a stale local internal balance generation.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only or reversible marker tied to stale internal balance visibility with no real token value or live-chain consequence.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate fake token generation, outer call, hook callback, old/new balance generations, guard state, consumer marker, outer commit, and receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold actor, token behavior, amount, callback target, and invariant constant while changing only internal balance commit before versus after the token call.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject token mock semantics outside contract, callback after balance commit, stale snapshot from another transaction, independent authorization, or nonshared balance state.
scenarios.evidence_level: SCR3 because a controlled depth-1 hook callback reaches a protected local consumer while it observes the wrong internal balance generation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SCR3 maximum until a bounded reversible protocol-state effect plus complete call/guard/continuation provenance justifies SCR4 or SCR5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A read-only callback observes a transient synthetic share/accounting value and a local mock consumer trusts that value for a bounded protected decision before the outer transaction finalizes.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A local test chain uses a read-only observer, synthetic share values, mock decision consumer, and inert decision markers with no asset transfer or production effect.
scenarios.positive_control: A consumer that revalidates the share/accounting value after callback completion uses the committed generation and produces the expected safe decision.
scenarios.negative_control: The same transient read with no downstream protected consumer remains an observation only and produces no decision marker.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would deploy against a live protocol, move real assets, use unbounded recursion, grief gas/resources, or leave the owned local test chain.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After the consumer revalidates at the committed state or the protocol prevents transient exposure, the read-only callback cannot drive a stale protected decision.
scenarios.outer_transaction_callback_generation: Record outer transaction, share-state pre-call generation, read-only callback generation, observer call frame, consumer decision generation, and final commit.
scenarios.external_call_reentrant_entry_trace: Bind the external callback trigger, read-only observer entrypoint, exact transient share value returned, and consumer invocation that receives it.
scenarios.transient_state_update_ordering: Capture expected share update order, transient share generation visible during callback, deferred outer writes, and committed value after return.
scenarios.lock_guard_invariant_scope: Record guard/phase state and whether the read-only observer or downstream consumer is allowed to rely on transient share values during the protected transition.
scenarios.cross_function_contract_hook_lineage: Classify the path as read-only callback observation and bind outer contract, observer, mock consumer, and any cross-contract lineage.
scenarios.outer_continuation_commit_state: Trace outer continuation, share/accounting commit, any revalidation, final state, and whether the earlier read-only decision survives after commit.
scenarios.downstream_protocol_consumer_identity: Identify the local mock decision consumer that accepts the transient share value and emits the bounded inert protected-decision marker.
scenarios.effective_reentrancy_state_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to influencing one local inert decision using a transient read-only share value during a bounded callback.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a deterministic inert decision receipt containing transient/committed share generations and no real financial or governance effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate outer transaction, observer callback, transient share value, consumer decision, outer continuation, committed share state, and final receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold deployment, observer, consumer, actor, and share transition constant while changing only consumption of transient value versus post-callback revalidation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject a consumer designed to use transient values, observer call after commit, unrelated share generation, cached value from another transaction, or unprotected decision semantics.
scenarios.evidence_level: SCR4 because an inert protected decision is causally bound to a read-only callback consuming transient synthetic share state before final commit.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SCR4 maximum until complete observer/consumer provenance, alternatives, remediation replay, and regression evidence satisfy SCR5.
